title: Stability of power-split completed presentations under perturbation
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and put $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ for $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in P$, put $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ and $B=P/J$, and suppose $B$ is $I$-adically complete. Let $K=(k_{j\ell})\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times t}(P)$, where $m,t\geq0$, and assume that the sequence $P^{\oplus t}\xrightarrow{K}P^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{(g_1,\ldots,g_m)}P\to B\to0$ is exact at $P^{\oplus m}$, $P$, and $B$. Let $\delta:J/J^2\to B^{\oplus r}$ send $f\bmod J^2$ to $(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, with derivatives extended continuously from polynomials. Suppose there is $c\geq0$ such that for every $a\in I^c$ there is a $B$-linear $h_a:B^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$ with $h_a\delta=a\operatorname{id}$. Then there is $N\geq1$ such that for every $g'_1,\ldots,g'_m\in P$ and $K'=(k'_{j\ell})\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times t}(P)$ satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^m g'_jk'_{j\ell}=0$ for every $\ell$, $g_j-g'_j\in I^NP$ for every $j$, and $k_{j\ell}-k'_{j\ell}\in I^NP$ for every $j,\ell$, there is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $B\cong P/(g'_1,\ldots,g'_m)$.

source.place: Tag 0GAR (lemma-close-enough); its rig-smooth hypothesis is written as the continuous conormal power-splitting criterion of lemma-equivalent-with-artin-smooth, condition (3). The missing completion hat in the printed definition of P is restored.

proof.text: Write $H=IP$. The polynomial algebra $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Its completion ideal is finitely generated, and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] makes $P$ $H$-adically complete with $P/H=(A/I)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] puts $H$ in every maximal ideal. For every ideal $J'\subseteq P$, the quotient $P/J'$ is Noetherian by the finite-type lemma over $P$, and is $H$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian], since it is generated as a $P$-module by $1$. The module completion and ring completion agree by their componentwise operations. In particular these facts hold for $B$ and every $B'=P/(g')$.

source.place: Tag 0GAR, preliminary hypotheses for (B) and the application of 0GAQ; Algebra Tags 0316, 05GG, 05GI, 00MA.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] over $P$ to $\operatorname{im}K\subseteq P^{\oplus m}$ and $J=\operatorname{im}g\subseteq P$. Choose a common enlarged bound $b\geq0$. If $u:U\to V$ is either $K$ or $g$, the resulting inclusion is $\operatorname{im}u\cap H^dV\subseteq u(H^{d-b}U)$ for $d\geq b$: lift each summand $ay$ in $H^{d-b}\operatorname{im}u$ to $ax$ with $u(x)=y$. Suppose a perturbed complex is congruent modulo $H^N$, with $N\geq b+1$. Apply [lem-sfb-perturbed-image-artin-rees-bound] to $(L,M,V,f,g,f',g')=(P^{\oplus t},P^{\oplus m},P,K,g,K',g')$. All modules are finite, $\operatorname{im}K=\ker g$ is assumed, $g' K'=0$ is assumed, $H$ lies in every maximal ideal by step 1, and coefficient congruence implies the required image congruences. Consequently $J'\cap H^d\subseteq g'(H^{d-b}P^{\oplus m})$ for every $d\geq b$.

source.place: Tag 07VE (lemma-approximate-complex), preservation of the right differential Artin-Rees bound; Algebra 00IN.

proof.text: For every $d\geq0$ we have $H^{d+1}+(J\cap H^d)=H^{d+1}+(J'\cap H^d)$. For $d\leq b$, replace $g(v)\in J\cap H^d$ by $g'(v)$: their difference lies in $H^N\subseteq H^{d+1}$, so the latter lies in $J'\cap H^d$. Interchanging the two rows proves the reverse inclusion. For $d>b$, step 2 writes $y\in J\cap H^d$ as $g(v)$ with $v\in H^{d-b}P^{\oplus m}$. Replacing it by $g'(v)$ changes it by an element of $H^{N+d-b}\subseteq H^{d+1}$. The perturbed bound in step 2 gives the reverse inclusion by the same explicit replacement. The degree-$d$ graded quotients of $B,B'$ are therefore the identical quotient $H^d/(H^{d+1}+J\cap H^d)=H^d/(H^{d+1}+J'\cap H^d)$. Sending a representative $p$ to that same $p$ commutes with addition and multiplication of representatives and with scalars from $A/I$. By the multiplication formula of [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure] these maps give a degree-preserving $A/I$-algebra isomorphism $E:\operatorname{gr}_I(B)\to\operatorname{gr}_I(B')$.

source.place: Tag 07VF (lemma-approximate-complex-graded), the common-subquotient calculation, with N=P.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-power-split-uniform-adic-map-lifting] to the given $A,I,P,J,B,c$ and reference target $C_0=B$. Step 1 supplies its Noetherian and completeness hypotheses and the power splitting is exactly the hypothesis of the item. Obtain $e\geq0$ and $n_0\geq e+1$, and set $N=\max(b+1,n_0)$. Fix any perturbation as in the statement and put $B'=P/J'$. The equality $J+I^NP=J'+I^NP$, obtained by replacing each generator by its congruent partner in both directions, gives an $A$-algebra map $\psi_N:B\to B'/I^NB'$ inducing the canonical isomorphism on the quotients modulo $I^N$. Steps 1 and 3 give the completeness and graded-isomorphism hypotheses for target $C=B'$ (use $E^{-1}$). The cited lifting lemma supplies $\varphi:B\to B'$ agreeing with $\psi_N$ modulo $I^{N-e}$, hence modulo $I$, since $N-e\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0GAR, (A), (C), choice of n and the paragraph applying Tag 0GAQ.

proof.text: Let $q:P\to B$ and $q':P\to B'$ be the quotient maps. Agreement modulo $I$ gives $\varphi(q(p))-q'(p)\in IB'$ for every $p\in P$. For $p\in H^d=I^dP$, write $p=\sum a_jp_j$ with $a_j\in I^d\subseteq A$. Since $\varphi$ is an $A$-algebra map, $\varphi(q(p))-q'(p)=\sum a_j(\varphi(q(p_j))-q'(p_j))\in I^{d+1}B'$. Thus on each graded piece the actual map induced by $\varphi$ is exactly the common-representative map $E$ of step 3. In particular it is injective in every degree; this checks the compatibility which the source leaves as a tiny argument.

source.place: Tag 0GAR, final paragraph, parenthetical alternative: the lifted map induces the isomorphism found above.

proof.text: The extension to $B'$ of the ideal $IB\subseteq B$ through $\varphi$ is exactly $IB'$: both are generated by the same images of $a\in I$, because $\varphi$ fixes $A$ and $1$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] applies to $R=B$, $S=B'$, ideal $IB$, and $f=\varphi$. The source is complete, the target is separated by step 1, and the map modulo the extended ideal is the canonical isomorphism from step 4. Therefore $\varphi$ is surjective. If $\varphi(z)=0$, induction on $d$ shows $z\in I^dB$: the case $d=0$ is tautological, and if $z\in I^dB$, injectivity on the degree-$d$ piece from step 5 forces $z\in I^{d+1}B$. The intersection of these powers is zero because $B\to\varprojlim B/I^dB$ is injective by completeness. Thus $z=0$, so $\varphi$ is also injective. Its set-theoretic inverse preserves sums, products, $1$ and $A$ by applying the injective map $\varphi$ to each required equality. This is the asserted $A$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GAR, final two paragraphs; Algebra 0315 for surjectivity; injectivity from separatedness.

It holds uniformly for every C whose associated graded ring is isomorphic to that of C_0, because d(S) and q(S) depend only on the graded ring up to isomorphism.
